studies.Study: Shivappa N et al. (2017) [PMID: 27693878] — estimate 1 · Mixed
studies.Reference: Dietary Inflammatory Index and Risk of Bladder Cancer in a Large Italian Case-control Study.
studies.Title: Dietary Inflammatory Index and Risk of Bladder Cancer in a Large Italian Case-control Study.
studies.Authors: Shivappa N, Hébert JR, Rosato V, Rossi M, Libra M, Montella M, Serraino D, La Vecchia C

combined_direction_harmonization.method: Reciprocal ratio and reversed reciprocal CI bounds, matching the saved source inversion flag.

studies.Population: Incident, histologically confirmed bladder cancer cases and cancer-free hospital controls from four areas in Italy
studies.comparison_type: highest versus lowest quartile of DII score (more pro-inflammatory versus anti-inflammatory diet)

sample_size.excerpt: Cases were 690 patients with incident, histologically confirmed cases of BC from 4 areas in Italy. Controls were 665 cancer free subjects admitted to the same network of hospitals as cases for a wide spectrum of acute, non-neoplastic conditions.
sample_size.location: Methods, Design and Participants; total_n derived from reported group counts 690 + 665 = 1355

cases.excerpt: Cases were 690 patients with incident, histologically confirmed cases of BC from 4 areas in Italy.

effect_size.excerpt: Subjects in the highest quartile of DII scores (ie, with a more pro-inflammatory diet) had a higher risk of BC compared to subjects in the lowest quartile (ie, with an anti-inflammatory diet) (OR<sub>Quartile4vs1</sub> = 1.97; 95% [confidence interval], 1.28, 3.03; P trend = .003).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Subjects in the highest quartile of DII scores (ie, with a more pro-inflammatory diet) had a higher risk of BC compared to subjects in the lowest quartile (ie, with an anti-inflammatory diet) (OR<sub>Quartile4vs1</sub> = 1.97; 95% [confidence interval], 1.28, 3.03; P trend = .003).

comparison.excerpt: Subjects in the highest quartile of DII scores (ie, with a more pro-inflammatory diet) had a higher risk of BC compared to subjects in the lowest quartile (ie, with an anti-inflammatory diet)

design.excerpt: In this study we explored the association between the dietary inflammatory index (DII) and BC risk in an Italian case-control study conducted between 2003 and 2014.

timing.excerpt: an Italian case-control study conducted between 2003 and 2014

exposure_measurement.excerpt: The DII was computed based on dietary intake assessed using a reproducible and valid 80-item food frequency questionnaire.

gender.excerpt: Odds ratios (OR) were estimated through logistic regression models adjusting for age, sex, total energy intake, and other recognized confounding factors.

studies.Study: Prado S et al. (2026) [PMID: 41914981] — estimate 1 · Mixed
studies.Reference: Anti-inflammatory Diet Index and Bladder Cancer Risk by Stage: A 22-Year Prospective Swedish Cohort Study (1998-2020).
studies.Title: Anti-inflammatory Diet Index and Bladder Cancer Risk by Stage: A 22-Year Prospective Swedish Cohort Study (1998-2020).
studies.Authors: Prado S, Ugge H, Vikerfors A, Fall K, Taj T
studies.Journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
studies.Population: Cohort of Swedish Men and Swedish Mammography Cohort participants
studies.comparison_type: Highest anti-inflammatory diet index quartile (Q4) versus lowest quartile (Q1)

sample_size.excerpt: The anti-inflammatory diet index (AIDI), composed of 16 food groups (11 anti- and 5 pro-inflammatory), was used to score dietary patterns in N = 79,292 individuals derived from the Cohort of Swedish Men (established in 1997) and the Swedish Mammography Cohort (established in 1987).

cases.excerpt: After a 22-year follow-up, 1,165 individuals were diagnosed with bladder cancer, of whom 249 had non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC), 201 had muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC), and 715 had unknown stage.

effect_size.excerpt: In repeated-measures analyses, the highest anti-inflammatory quartile (Q4) was associated with lower bladder cancer risk compared with the lowest quartile [Q1; HR, 0.74; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.61-0.89].

confidence_interval.excerpt: In repeated-measures analyses, the highest anti-inflammatory quartile (Q4) was associated with lower bladder cancer risk compared with the lowest quartile [Q1; HR, 0.74; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.61-0.89].

timing.excerpt: Dietary information was collected in 1997 and 2009; repeated-measures analyses used a cumulative-average AIDI.
